summary: ```markdown # How to Create Pockets in Marvelous Designer ## Introduction Hello everyone! In this tutorial video, we will learn how to make pockets in Marvelous Designer. ## Creating a Basic Pocket First, let's make a basic pocket. Since we want to sew the pockets onto the clothes, we need to use the inner rectangle on the clothing to drag the pattern of the pocket. Click on it and drag to create a rectangle. Alternatively, you can use the inner rectangle tool; click the left button to enter the exact dimensions for creation. After creating the rectangle, use the adjustment tool to drag the inner rectangle and adjust the position of the pocket. You can also shrink the pattern if necessary. Next, right-click to select the rectangle as the pattern, and place it in the 2D and 3D windows. After arranging them, use the line sewing tool to click on the lines of the panel and the pocket panel we have extracted. Sew the three sides together, leaving the top edge unsewn. Now, turn on the simulation. The sewing line function will sew this pocket together. Since there is no sewing line at the top, it remains open, resulting in a simple pocket. ## Increasing Pocket Thickness Next, let's explore how to increase the thickness of this pocket. It's important to understand that when we increase the thickness, only the three sewn edges will increase. To do this, we will use the edge panel tool to select these three edges separately. Right-click and select "Panel Outline Expansion" to adjust the thickness of the side edges. Note that our diameter and expansion number are essential. The diameter refers to the width of the side edge. If we want to expand, we can start by entering "1". Remember to select the inner line to continue making adjustments to the original rectangular edges. The side angle will be the default angle in this situation. In other words, they will extend together. We need to switch it to five corners so that the expanded part will not link together. Press the control key and turn on the simulation to view the changes. You will see that the thickness of the side edge is automatically applied as the side panel has been expanded. ## Sewing the Sides Together Next, we need to sew the two sides together. If we turn on the simulation and drag the panel, we will notice that the side edges are not yet sewn together. Use the edge panel tool to sew them up. Then, adjust the fold angle of the inner line generated from the panel outline expansion from the default of 180 to 0. This adjustment will position the inner lines at the front of the panel, resulting in a rounded and angular fold. Next, we choose to expand the panel outline and the inner line simultaneously. Right-click and select "Generate Inner Line According to the Line" to create a fold line in the middle of the two lines. After creating it, simulate and apply the changes. Now we will prepare for the effect of folding pockets. Ensure that the display method in the 3D space is set to "Texture Surface" to distinguish the shape of the panel. ## Folding the Pocket Now, we need to fold the middle line inward. Set the folding angle to 360 degrees. If the folding angle applied to the inner line exceeds 180 degrees, it will fold inward. To smooth the isolation effect of the panel, we first reduce the particle diameter and simulate it again. When we adjust the view, we will see that the pocket now has a folding effect. ## Raising the Bottom of the Pocket Next, let's learn how to raise the bottom of the pocket. First, we will use the editor to delete the horizontal line. Then, we need to fold it up by removing the foldable position. Select the plus point line tool and right-click on the two original panel lines to enter specific values. For the line length, we will enter "5 mm", which is half the length of the panel line we just created. After adding a point, select the endpoint of the middle line and drag it to this point. Note that during this process, the bottom point does not change. Thus, we need to select the three inner lines in the middle, right-click, and choose "Increase Point to the Panel Line" to automatically create a breakpoint on the panel line. Now, drag and select the frame in the 2D window along with the breakpoint of the inner line and the point on the panel line. Adjust it according to the pink straight line corresponding to the previous line. In the 3D window, we will see that the side has been processed, and the position of the bottom is the same. Repeat the same process on the other side. You can directly drag the point we have created, or right-click to enter a specific value. ## Sewing the Gaps Now that we have a triangular position with defined lengths on each side, we can sew the two sides of the gap together. After opening the simulation, the panels will automatically come together. Then, press Shift + Q to hide the panel on the back, and Shift + A to hide the virtual model. Upon closer inspection of the inside of the pocket, we will notice that although the gaps are sewn together, they are not sewn in the middle. To fix this, we need to use the line sewing tool on both sides, ensuring the correct direction. After sewing, press the control key to simulate. If you are unsure of the direction, you can use the blue point in the three bottom windows to match. ## Final Adjustments Now that it is sewn up and in a folded state, we need to ensure that the bottom of the pocket is tighter. In real life, the bottom of a square-shaped pocket often has an oblique line on the side to attach it to the pants. We will use the internal multidirectional line tool according to the two straight lines we created earlier to draw an oblique inner line. Then, we will use the line powder tool to sew them up on the left and right, securing the bottom of the pocket. Next, we will draw the necessary lines on the clothing. Use the internal multidirectional line tool while holding the Shift key to create a line along the corner. If you want to change the length of the line, use the plus point division function (shortcut key X). On the inner line, right-click to enter the same value we previously set, which is 5 mm. Then, use the internal multidirectional line tool to draw an oblique line and sew these two inner lines together. This will ensure that the corner of the bottom of the pocket is secured to the body. If we want to lengthen this inner line, we can drag this point with the editor. During the dragging process, hold the Ctrl key to extend it along the original rhythm. You can also right-click to enter specific values. Now, the inner line is aligned correctly, and we can move the bottom of this line to the blue point, ensuring equal positioning. ## Conclusion Finally, we have completed the process of creating the pocket. Remember that when creating, attention to detail is crucial to ensure that all edges align correctly. You can also use the edit board function to make adjustments. If you have any questions, feel free to ask in the comments. Thank you for watching! ```
